items.stem:

The John Lewis Partnership (UK) is owned in trust for its employees, called Partners, who share in profits through an annual bonus.

Explain why cooperatives may have more motivated workers. Refer to the extract or to another organization you have studied. [4]
items.answer: Workers are owners who share profits and vote on decisions, so they have a stake in the success of the business and a voice in how it is run.

items.stem:
Paper 1 (d). Toyota production workers meet in small teams to suggest improvements; the company receives hundreds of thousands of suggestions a year.

"Non-financial rewards are more effective than financial rewards in motivating employees." With reference to Toyota's quality circles, discuss this statement. [10]
items.answer: Non-financial rewards are more effective once pay is fair; the best approach combines both and fits the job and workforce.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: meet higher-level needs; long-lasting motivation (Herzberg, Pink); lower cost than pay rises. Arguments against: employees need adequate pay first; some workers prefer money; job enrichment is not possible in all jobs; empowerment needs skills and trust. items.stem:
Many fast-growing firms, such as some UK fintech and food-delivery start-ups in 2021-22, have struggled to fund rapid expansion despite rising sales.

The board must decide whether to act on the view that cash flow is more important than profit for a business. Recommend a course of action, weighing the arguments for and against. [10]
items.answer: Cash flow is more important in the short run for survival; profit is more important in the long run for sustainability and growth.
items.markingKey: Supporting: lack of cash causes insolvency; needed to pay wages and suppliers; start-ups fail through cash shortages. Challenging: long-run survival requires profit; profit attracts investors and finance; cash can be borrowed if profitable. Recommendation: Cash flow is more important in the short run for survival; profit is more important in the long run for sustainability and growth. items.stem: Café Andino had opening inventory of £40,000 and closing inventory of £50,000. Cost of sales for the year was £240,000. Calculate the stock turnover (number of times per year).
items.answer: 5.3 times
items.markingKey: Average stock = (40,000 + 50,000)/2 = 45,000; turnover = cost of sales / average stock = 5.3. [M1] for a correct formula/method with substituted values; [A1] for 5.3 times. Units (%, $, days, times) required for [A1]. Apply own figure rule (OFR) to later parts.

items.stem: Tasman Surf Co. has cash of £5,000, trade receivables of £20,000, inventories of £30,000, trade payables of £40,000 and a bank overdraft of £25,000, all due within 30 days. Calculate the current ratio and the acid-test ratio, and comment on the risk that the business becomes insolvent.
items.answer: Current ratio = 55,000/65,000 = 0.85:1; acid-test = 25,000/65,000 = 0.38:1. Liquid assets do not cover current liabilities, so it may be unable to pay its debts as they fall due unless it sells stock quickly – a real risk of insolvency.
items.markingKey: current assets 55,000; current liabilities 65,000; ratios 0.85 and 0.38. [M1] for a correct formula/method with substituted values; [A1] for both ratios. Units (%, $, days, times) required for [A1]. Apply own figure rule (OFR) to later parts. [1] comment on insolvency risk.

items.stem: Mekong Furniture's budget and actual results for the quarter were: sales revenue: budget £360,000, actual £378,000; raw materials: budget £25,000, actual £26,250; wages: budget £40,000, actual £44,000; marketing: budget £20,000, actual £18,000; rent: budget £60,000, actual £54,000. Calculate the variance for each item, stating whether each is favourable or adverse, and the profit variance. Suggest two possible reasons for the variances.
items.answer: sales revenue £18,000 favourable; raw materials £1,250 adverse; wages £4,000 adverse; marketing £2,000 favourable; rent £6,000 favourable. Budgeted profit £215,000, actual profit £235,750: profit variance £20,750 favourable. Possible reasons: changes in demand or prices, supplier price changes, overtime, unplanned marketing campaigns, inaccurate budgets.
items.markingKey: Variance = actual − budget; revenue above budget and costs below budget are favourable. [M1] for a correct formula/method with substituted values; [A1] for all variances and the profit variance. Units (%, $, days, times) required for [A1]. Apply own figure rule (OFR) to later parts. [R1][R1] reasons.

items.stem:

items.answer: Effective leaders adapt their style to the situation, although democratic approaches generally suit knowledge-based organizations.

The board must decide whether to act on the view that trade unions benefit businesses as well as employees. Recommend a course of action, weighing the arguments for and against. [10]
items.answer: Unions can benefit firms where relations are cooperative; the outcome depends on management's approach and the union's willingness to work in partnership.

items.stem: With reference to one or two organizations you have studied, examine how the concept of change affects the claim that leadership is more important than management for the success of a business. [20]
items.answer: Both are essential: leadership matters most in times of change and innovation, management in stable, efficiency-driven operations.
items.markingKey: Concept: change. Arguments for: vision and motivation drive innovation; leaders guide change; culture and engagement. Arguments against: without planning and control, resources are wasted; routine operations depend on management; depends on the situation and industry. Possible conclusion: Both are essential: leadership matters most in times of change and innovation, management in stable, efficiency-driven operations. BM concept markbands [20], five criteria: A knowledge and understanding of the concept and content (4); B application to a real organization (4); C reasoned arguments supported by evidence (4); D structure (4); E individuals and societies – perspectives of different stakeholders (4). Top band in each: precise, well-integrated, balanced and substantiated; the concept (change, creativity, ethics or sustainability) shapes the whole answer.

items.stem: Using the concept of change, discuss the view that the growth of the gig economy benefits both businesses and workers. Refer to at least one real organization you have studied. [20]

items.stem: The statement of financial position of Andes Alpaca Wear shows current assets made up of stock £50,000, debtors £40,000 and cash £5,000; current liabilities total £80,000. Calculate the current ratio.
items.markingKey: Current ratio = current assets / current liabilities = 95,000/80,000 = 1.19. [M1] for a correct formula/method with substituted values; [A1] for 1.19:1. Units (%, $, days, times) required for [A1]. Apply own figure rule (OFR) to later parts.

items.stem: Atlas Print made a profit before tax of $360,000. Corporation tax is 25% and the directors pay out 40% of profit after tax as dividends. There are 100,000 shares. Calculate profit after tax, total dividends, retained profit and the dividend per share.
items.answer: Tax = $90,000; profit after tax = $270,000; dividends = $108,000; retained profit = $162,000; dividend per share = $1.08.
items.markingKey: 360,000 × 25% = 90,000; 360,000 − 90,000 = 270,000; 40% × 270,000 = 108,000; 270,000 − 108,000 = 162,000; 108,000/100,000 = 1.08. [M1] for a correct formula/method with substituted values; [A1] for all four values. Units (%, $, days, times) required for [A1]. Apply own figure rule (OFR) to later parts.

items.stem: Kiwi Fresh's budget and actual results for the quarter were: sales revenue: budget €400,000, actual €420,000; raw materials: budget €20,000, actual €22,000; wages: budget €20,000, actual €24,000; marketing: budget €10,000, actual €9,000; rent: budget €25,000, actual €21,250. Calculate the variance for each item, stating whether each is favourable or adverse, and the profit variance. Suggest two possible reasons for the variances.
items.answer: sales revenue €20,000 favourable; raw materials €2,000 adverse; wages €4,000 adverse; marketing €1,000 favourable; rent €3,750 favourable. Budgeted profit €325,000, actual profit €343,750: profit variance €18,750 favourable. Possible reasons: changes in demand or prices, supplier price changes, overtime, unplanned marketing campaigns, inaccurate budgets.
items.markingKey: Variance = actual − budget; revenue above budget and costs below budget are favourable. [M1] for a correct formula/method with substituted values; [A1] for all variances and the profit variance. Units (%, $, days, times) required for [A1]. Apply own figure rule (OFR) to later parts. [R1][R1] reasons.

items.stem:
Silicon Valley Bank failed in March 2023 after depositors withdrew $42 bn in a day; its bond holdings had lost value as interest rates rose.

Using the extract where relevant, analyse the advantages and disadvantages of acting on the view that ratio analysis is of limited value in predicting business failure. [8]
items.answer: Ratios give useful warnings, especially in trends, but predicting failure also requires cash-flow forecasts and qualitative judgement.
items.markingKey: Advantages: historical data; window dressing; qualitative factors omitted; failure often sudden. Disadvantages: trends in liquidity and gearing give early warnings; used by lenders and investors; combined ratios (e.g. Altman Z-score) predict failure. 7-8: balanced analysis applied to the case; 5-6: analysis of both sides, partly applied; 3-4: one-sided or generic; 1-2: descriptive.

items.stem:
British sports car maker Morgan builds only around 800 hand-made cars a year at its Malvern factory.

Using the information and your knowledge of business management, evaluate whether small businesses are more successful than large businesses, and recommend what the organization should do. [10]
items.answer: Neither size is inherently better; success depends on the market, the objectives of the owners and how well the business uses the advantages of its size.
items.markingKey: Supporting: flexibility and customer focus; niche markets; lower overheads. Challenging: lack of economies of scale; difficulty raising finance; vulnerable to competition and shocks; success depends on the market and owner objectives. Recommendation: Neither size is inherently better; success depends on the market, the objectives of the owners and how well the business uses the advantages of its size. BM markbands [10]: 9-10 – relevant knowledge and understanding; terms defined; effective use of the case/stimulus and relevant business management tools; balanced analysis of advantages and disadvantages for stakeholders; a reasoned, substantiated judgement or recommendation. 7-8 – good understanding and use of the case, balanced analysis, judgement partly substantiated. 5-6 – some understanding, analysis mostly one-sided or not fully linked to the case, limited judgement. 3-4 – limited understanding, mostly descriptive. 1-2 – little relevant knowledge. Answers without explicit reference to the case or organization cannot reach the top bands.

items.stem: With reference to one or two organizations you have studied, examine how the concept of ethics affects the claim that debt factoring is the best way for a small business to solve cash-flow problems. [20]
items.answer: Factoring helps quickly where receivables are large, but cheaper solutions such as better credit control or an overdraft may be preferable.
items.markingKey: Concept: ethics. Arguments for: immediate cash; factor manages collection; no new debt. Arguments against: costly – loses a percentage of receivables; customers may see it as a sign of weakness; does not solve underlying problems; only works if the firm has receivables. Possible conclusion: Factoring helps quickly where receivables are large, but cheaper solutions such as better credit control or an overdraft may be preferable. BM concept markbands [20], five criteria: A knowledge and understanding of the concept and content (4); B application to a real organization (4); C reasoned arguments supported by evidence (4); D structure (4); E individuals and societies – perspectives of different stakeholders (4). Top band in each: precise, well-integrated, balanced and substantiated; the concept (change, creativity, ethics or sustainability) shapes the whole answer.

items.stem:
Paper 3 (a). Mondragon is a federation of worker cooperatives in the Basque Country, employing around 70,000 people, where worker-members own the businesses and vote on major decisions.

Describe the human need that Mondragon Corporation (Spain) is addressing. [2]
items.answer: Secure, democratic employment and a fair share of the value workers create
items.markingKey: [1] for identifying the human need (secure, democratic employment and a fair share of the value workers create); [1] for describing it with reference to the case.

items.stem:
Paper 3 (b). Aravind, founded in 1976 in Madurai, performs hundreds of thousands of cataract operations a year; paying patients cross-subsidise free or low-cost surgery for the poor using assembly-line style processes.

Explain why the results of a decision tree may be unreliable. Where relevant, apply your answer to Aravind Eye Care System (India). [4]
items.answer: Probabilities and financial outcomes are estimates that may be biased or wrong, and the tree ignores qualitative factors and managers' attitudes to risk.
items.markingKey: Probabilities and financial outcomes are estimates that may be biased or wrong, and the tree ignores qualitative factors and managers' attitudes to risk. Award [2] for a relevant explanation and [2] for applying it to the social enterprise and its human need (access to affordable eye care to prevent avoidable blindness).

items.stem:
Paper 3 (c). SELCO, founded in Bengaluru in 1995, sells and finances solar lighting and energy systems for low-income households and micro-enterprises, often through partnerships with rural banks.

Using the example of the UK HS2 railway (Cost estimates for the UK's HS2 high-speed railway rose from about £33 bn in 2010 to well over £60 bn for a shortened route, and the northern leg was cancelled in 2023.) as a comparison, analyse how investment appraisal of long-term projects could apply to SELCO India. [4]
items.answer: Rising costs and distant benefits reduce the present value of large infrastructure projects Applied to SELCO India: the same logic must be adapted to its social mission (reliable, affordable energy (lighting and power) for households without a stable electricity supply), limited resources and stakeholders.
items.markingKey: [2] for a relevant, explained point about investment appraisal of long-term projects; [2] for applying it to SELCO India and its human need. Rising costs and distant benefits reduce the present value of large infrastructure projects

items.stem:
Paper 3 (d). Who Gives A Crap sells recycled and bamboo toilet paper online and donates 50% of its profits to charities building toilets and sanitation in developing countries.

To meet its human need, Who Gives A Crap (Australia) is considering two options for distribution:
Option 1: sell through major supermarket chains.
Option 2: remain online-only with subscription deliveries.

Using the case and your knowledge of business management, recommend which option Who Gives A Crap (Australia) should choose. [15]
items.answer: A justified recommendation of one option weighing: margins and the share of profit donated; brand values and customer loyalty; volume growth; supermarket power; environmental footprint of delivery.
items.markingKey: Relevant considerations: margins and the share of profit donated; brand values and customer loyalty; volume growth; supermarket power; environmental footprint of delivery. Human need: access to safe sanitation for the roughly 3.5 billion people without safely managed sanitation. Either option can be recommended if justified. Paper 3 recommendation markbands [15]: 13-15 – a clear recommendation of one option, justified with the case and relevant tools; both options weighed against the human need and the social enterprise's resources and stakeholders; limitations of the data acknowledged. 10-12 – recommendation supported, analysis of both options but uneven. 7-9 – some analysis, recommendation partly justified. 4-6 – mostly descriptive. 1-3 – little relevant content.
